From 2c58070fde0fffe494d9e38b0ccedbda01c512ff Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Chen Ni <nichen@iscas.ac.cn>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2024 11:07:25 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] watchdog: lenovo_se10_wdt: Convert comma to semicolon

Replace a comma between expression statements by a semicolon.

Fixes: 1f6602c8ed1e ("watchdog: lenovo_se10_wdt: Watchdog driver for Lenovo SE10 platform")
Signed-off-by: Chen Ni <nichen@iscas.ac.cn>
Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Reviewed-by: Mark Pearson <mpearson-lenovo@squebb.ca>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240716030725.400400-1-nichen@iscas.ac.cn
Signed-off-by: Guenter Roeck <linux@roeck-us.net>
Signed-off-by: Wim Van Sebroeck <wim@linux-watchdog.org>

diff --git a/drivers/watchdog/lenovo_se10_wdt.c b/drivers/watchdog/lenovo_se10_wdt.c
index 139ff0e8220f..cd0500e5080b 100644
--- a/drivers/watchdog/lenovo_se10_wdt.c
+++ b/drivers/watchdog/lenovo_se10_wdt.c
@@ -196,8 +196,8 @@ static int se10_wdt_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 	watchdog_set_drvdata(&priv->wdd, priv);
 
 	priv->wdd.parent = dev;
-	priv->wdd.info = &wdt_info,
-	priv->wdd.ops = &se10_wdt_ops,
+	priv->wdd.info = &wdt_info;
+	priv->wdd.ops = &se10_wdt_ops;
 	priv->wdd.timeout = WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT; /* Set default timeout */
 	priv->wdd.min_timeout = MIN_TIMEOUT;
 	priv->wdd.max_timeout = MAX_TIMEOUT;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/watchdog/lenovo_se10_wdt.c`**
- Changed the syntax from using a comma to a semicolon in two lines of code:
  - Line with `priv->wdd.info = &wdt_info,` was modified to `priv->wdd.info = &wdt_info;`
  - Line with `priv->wdd.ops = &se10_wdt_ops,` was modified to `priv->wdd.ops = &se10_wdt_ops;`

### Relationships
The modifications in the file are related to correcting the syntax of the code. The original use of commas in the assignment statements was incorrect and could lead to unintended behavior. By replacing the commas with semicolons, the code now properly terminates each statement, ensuring that the assignments are executed correctly. This change is part of a bug fix for a previously identified issue in the watchdog driver for the Lenovo SE10 platform.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
priv->wdd.info = &wdt_info,
priv->wdd.ops = &se10_wdt_ops,
```
Reason:
The use of a comma instead of a semicolon in the assignment statements improperly terminates the first statement, causing the second assignment to be interpreted as part of the first. This can lead to unexpected behavior during execution, as the compiler may not correctly parse the intended assignments, potentially resulting in runtime errors or incorrect functionality in the watchdog driver.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
priv->wdd.info = &wdt_info;
priv->wdd.ops = &se10_wdt_ops;
```
Reason:
Replacing the comma with a semicolon correctly terminates each assignment statement, ensuring that the compiler interprets them as separate statements. This fixes the parsing issue and ensures that the watchdog driver functions as intended, preventing any unexpected behavior or errors during execution.
